fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Open Green Space; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Turnaround Space; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the access drive so emergency vehicles can travel its full length without obstruction.
• Clear vegetation on both sides of the access drive to allow two people to walk alongside a vehicle without stepping into brush.
• Cut back dense vegetation growing close to the main residence to create open ground between the plants and the exterior walls.
• Cut back dense vegetation growing close to the detached structure to create open ground between the plants and the exterior walls.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings on foot.
• Remove or reposition landscaping features that block direct foot access around the perimeter of the main residence.
• Mark the outer edge of the driveway near the end point so drivers know where usable surface ends before turnaround space runs out.
• Create a widened area or cleared pad at or near the end of the drive large enough for an emergency vehicle to turn around.
• Keep any gate or barrier at the single driveway entrance unlocked or equipped with a Knox-style lock box for immediate responder entry.
• Thin dense vegetation between the access drive and the open green space so responders can use that area for staging or secondary movement if the drive is blocked.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Long Driveway; Limited Rear Access; Scattered Trees; Grass Cover; Limited Turnaround Area; Single Access Route
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back shrubs and low branches that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house on all sides.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open gaps between individual trees and between the trees and the house.
• Remove low-hanging branches from scattered trees close to the house so fire cannot climb from ground vegetation up into the tree canopy.
• Cut or mow grass cover around the house and near the driveway regularly, especially during dry months.
• Clear mixed vegetation growing close to the foundation and along the walls of the house.
• Keep the full length of the driveway clear of overhanging branches so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Thin or remove shrubs and vegetation growing along the driveway edges that could narrow the travel lane.
• Create a wider cleared area at or near the house to give vehicles a place to turn around, using the existing space as much as possible.
• Clear vegetation from the rear of the property to open movement and visibility around the back of the house.
• Remove any dead plant material, dry grass, or brush piled near the house or outbuildings.
• Keep the area at the end of the driveway and near the house entrance free of vegetation so it remains usable as a staging area.
• Post the address visibly at the road entry point so the property can be located quickly from the single access route
